data.title: Commerce releases tools to optimize product catalogs for AI discovery
data.description:
Commerce has released two artificial intelligence tools to help merchants make their product catalogs ready for AI discovery.

It calls the tools Feedonomics Enrichment and BigCommerce Catalog Enrichment, noting that the capabilities serve both B2B and B2C merchants. Commerce described the tools as agentic commerce solutions, or its products and capabilities to help merchants prepare their product data for agentic AI discovery. The enrichment capabilities also help merchants connect AI tools to their business, enabling merchants to enable agentic shopping experiences, according to Commerce.

“AI agents can only answer questions about your products as well as your data allows,” said Sharon Gee, senior vice president of product for AI at Commerce, in an announcement. “Whether you’re a marketer driving AEO or a product leader building shopping agents, better data is the foundation for better agentic experiences. Feedonomics Enrichment and BigCommerce Catalog Enrichment give brands on any platform a data pipeline that lifts performance everywhere agents meet shoppers from Google to OpenAI and on their own sites and agents.”

The companies that come to Commerce are typically “deep in B2B and in enterprise retail,” Gee told Digital Commerce 360 separately. Consumers and B2B buyers are asking AI products to compare products, answer questions and — more recently — make purchases.

Commerce is the parent company of BigCommerce, Feedonomics, and Makeswift.

Retailers in the Top 2000 Database that used Commerce as their ecommerce platform in 2025 generated more than $538 billion in online sales that year. The Top 2000 Database is a market research tool tracking North America’s largest online retailers by their annual web sales. It also tracks the leading vendors those retailers use for their ecommerce technology stacks.

What Commerce’s AI product catalog enrichment tools do

Commerce said its enrichment tools “turn the product information a brand already has into more robust, consistent data.” The Feedonomics and BigCommerce tools both generate:

  • product titles
  • descriptions
  • feature bullets
  • frequently asked questions (FAQs)
  • search engine optimization (SEO) metadata

In addition, they produce facts, snippets and question-and-answer (Q&A) fields that generative AI platforms can use to interpret products. That process helps to determine what a product is, identify its target audience and determine its relevance to a user.

Commerce said the enrichment process creates complete records that give human shoppers and AI agents consistent details across storefronts, marketplaces, answer engines and other channels. It also removes the need for CSV exports and third-party tools, according to Commerce.

Gee offered the example that a retailer might need to translate its footwear catalog to 15 languages. It then needs to send each of those translations to:

  • Amazon
  • eBay
  • Google
  • Meta
  • TikTok
  • Walmart

Now, in addition, retailers also need to send those translations to answer engine channels such as ChatGPT, Claude, CoPilot, Gemini and Perplexity.

“You need to be able to have UCP support for each of them,” Gee said. “It’s a one-to-many problem — scale.”

The BigCommerce enrichment tool allows merchants to make self-serve enhancements to their product content. Meanwhile, the Feedonomics enrichment tool offers both self-manage and managed-service models.

How B2B companies are using Commerce

Merchants also go to Commerce because they want the technology and tooling for B2B as well as their B2C capabilities, Gee said.

She also noted that hybrid businesses — those selling both B2B and B2C — often need flexibility and composability in their technology stacks.

“It’s fairly trivial to sell things online anymore,” Gee said. “That’s a well-solved problem over the past two decades. There are many use cases that have not been solved well yet.”

One such problem is keying in manual purchase orders, which can have thousands of line items. Gee said an AI agent can complete that work in a “very short amount of time,” whereas it would take a human hours. Commerce’s Purchase Order Agent, she said, allows users to drag and drop a PDF into it. From there, the agent will automatically build a cart.

“Now those humans could get back to doing human work instead of rote, nasty data entry that is super manual that doesn’t actually add more value,” Gee said.

data.title: Amazon brings back Prime Big Deal Days in first week of October
data.description:
Amazon is bringing back its Prime Big Deal Days promotion, its sales event in October, continuing its recent approach of holding a sale in spring, summer and fall.

Like the summer iteration of the event, both Prime Day and Prime Big Deal Days are member-exclusive promotions. Amazon is offering early deals ahead of Prime Big Deal Days. Those include discounts on Amazon devices, Kindle, Amazon Music Unlimited and Amazon Haul.

Amazon Haul is the merchant’s storefront for budget-conscious consumers, focusing on ultra-low prices. The marketplace launched that storefront in beta in November 2024 as a competitor to Shein and Temu.

“Once fall arrives, there’s so much to get ready for — the hosting, the decorating, the holiday gifting — and Prime Big Deal Days makes it easy to check it all off while saving,” said Carmen Nestares, vice president of North America Marketing and Prime Tech, in an announcement.

For the first two years, in 2015 and 2026, Amazon Prime Day was exclusively a 24-hour sales event during the summer. From 2017 through 2024, it was a two-day event. Last year, it ran for four days, and Amazon has planned the same length for summer 2026.

Amazon ranks No. 1 in Digital Commerce 360’s Top 2000 Database. The database is how Digital Commerce 360 tracks the largest North American online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales.

Amazon is also No. 3 in Digital Commerce 360’s Global Online Marketplaces Database. That database ranks the 100 largest such marketplaces by third-party gross merchandise value (GMV).

When is Amazon Prime Day 2026?

In 2026, the Amazon Prime Big Deal Days event will run 48 hours, between Oct. 6 and 7. That’s nearly the same time frame as in 2025, when the event ran Oct. 7 and 8.

This year’s Prime Big Deal Days event will feature new product drops three times a day, according to Amazon:

  • Midnight PDT
  • 8 a.m.
  • 1 p.m.

Amazon said brands including Shark, Princess Polly and Soundcore will participate in the drops.

Amazon said members can find deals on Halloween products, for game-day and fall hosting, as well as for holiday gifting. It gave examples of costumes and accessories for as low as $5, candy for less than $10, charcuterie boards, slow cookers and a list of top toys.

Members can use Alexa for Shopping to set up deal and price alerts, as well as for auto-buying. Shoppers can also check price history on products or ask Alexa for Shopping to see up to 365 days of pricing insights.

Amazon released Alexa for Shopping in mid-May 2026. It serves as an artificial intelligence (AI) agent that combines Amazon’s Rufus and Alexa+ offerings. In June, Amazon added customized product designs within Alexa for Shopping, for certain merchandise.

During the summer, the Amazon Prime Day sales event ran for four days, from June 23 through June 26. That was just the second time that Amazon held its main Prime Day event of the year in June, as the retailer has most often opted for July.

The last time it made that decision was in 2021. Aside from that year and 2020 — when the COVID-19 pandemic shifted summer strategies — the summer iterations of the Amazon Prime Day event have always been in the middle of July. 

Prior to that, its most recent Prime Day-equivalent, Big Spring Sale, ran at the end of March 2026. It lasted for one week, from March 25 through 31.

 


How much did Amazon make on Prime Day?

Although Amazon did not attach a dollar amount to its summer 2026 Prime Day sales, it said the event was its biggest ever.

Digital Commerce 360 previously reported that during the time frame of the summer Prime Day event, U.S. ecommerce sales outside of Amazon reached $26.4 billion. That outdid Prime Day 2025’s impact, generating $24.1 billion in nationwide ecommerce sales.

As a comparison point, U.S. consumers spent $32.45 billion online across Thanksgiving, Black Friday and Cyber Monday  in 2025. Those were three of the largest days of that year in terms of online retail sales.

How many countries will Prime Day take place in?

Amazon Prime Big Deal Days will take place in 22 countries:

  1. Austria
  2. Belgium
  3. Canada
  4. Colombia
  5. Egypt
  6. France
  7. Germany
  8. Ireland
  9. Italy
  10. Luxembourg
  11. Mexico
  12. Netherlands
  13. Poland
  14. Portugal
  15. Saudi Arabia
  16. Singapore
  17. Spain
  18. Sweden
  19. Turkey
  20. United Arab Emirates
  21. United Kingdom
  22. United States

Amazon said Prime members in Australia, Brazil, India and Japan will be able to shop Prime Day deals later in the summer.

When is Amazon Prime Day usually?

Dates for Amazon Prime Day event in the past:

  • 12th: June 23-26, 2026
  • 11th: July 8-11, 2025
  • 10th: July 16-July 17, 2024
  • Ninth: July 11-12, 2023
  • Eighth: July 12-13, 2022
  • Seventh: June 21-22, 2021
  • Sixth: Oct 13-14, 2020
  • Fifth: July 15-16, 2019
  • Fourth: July 16-17, 2018
  • Third: July 11-12, 2017
  • Second: July 12, 2016
  • First: July 15, 2015

How often is Amazon Prime Day?

Until 2022, Amazon Prime Day was once a year in the summer. In 2022, the retail giant added another Prime Day event in October. So how many times a year is Prime Day? The answer used to be once. Amazon then established a two-year pattern of two separate sales events.

As of 2024, Amazon held its inaugural Big Spring Sale, from March 20 through 25. That Big Spring Sale event was open to all customers, and Prime members received access to exclusive deals, Amazon said.

Currently, the answer is that Amazon Prime Day — in its various sales event forms — is three times a year.

How do you sign up for a Prime membership?

You can join Prime or start a free trial at Amazon Prime Day. Amazon has recently faced a lawsuit from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission alleging the ecommerce giant duped consumers into signing up for its Prime membership service and deliberately made it hard to cancel. 

How to prepare to find deals on Prime Day 

The value of Prime Day to retailers both small and large is undisputed, as millions of shoppers visit the site in search of once-a-year deals.

  • Sign up for the Prime Insider newsletter to hear about Amazon Prime member benefits and find updates on deals and events.
  • Create deal alerts for recommendations. As an Amazon Prime Member, you can subscribe to receive deal alert notifications related to recent Amazon searches and recently viewed items. All you have to do is visit the Prime Day event page on the Amazon app before Prime Day to create deal alerts. Once Prime Day arrives, members will receive push notifications on any available deals.
  • Get deal notifications from Alexa. Alexa can make sure you don’t miss any Amazon deals. Members can add products to their Wish List, Cart, or Save for Later, and then ask Alexa to notify them about the deal.
  • Set a reminder so you don’t miss the multi-day event.
  • Check back here to see the latest updates.

What are the Big Spring Sale and Big Deal Days, and how are they different from Prime Days?

Amazon called its inaugural March promotional period its Big Spring Sale. In October 2023, it created a new fall sale event called Big Deal Days. Amazon’s Big Spring Sale is not exclusive to Prime members. The online retailer also held a fall sale in 2022 for the first time, called the Early Access Sale.

Prime Day is now Amazon’s biggest sale of the year. It is usually held during the summer months. In 2025, it was July 8 through July 11. Historically, the annual event has been two days and for Prime members only. 

Prime Day, which features deals on many products on Amazon.com, began in 2015 as a celebration of Amazon’s 20th year in business. It turned into a summer sales holiday to drum up additional business for Amazon — and the retailer’s marketplace sellers — before the holiday shopping season. In recent years, other large retailers have offered promotions on their own websites around Prime Day to take advantage of the additional online shoppers.

Abbas Haleem, Brian Warmoth, Mary Meisenzahl, James Risley and Paul Conley contributed to this report.

data.title: Puma, Maersk expand distribution relationship in North America
data.description:
A.P. Moller-Maersk has begun managing the North American distribution network for consumer brand manufacturer Puma.

Puma and Maersk said their “partnership has expanded well beyond ocean shipping.” Maersk is now operating more than 2 million square feet of Puma’s distribution network, including automated warehouses in Arizona, California and Indiana.

Helmut Leibbrandt, senior vice president of supply chain management and logistics for the Americas at Puma, said in a statement that the retailer requires an “agile, efficient” supply chain.

“As we’ve expanded our relationship with Maersk, we’ve seen the value of combining our highly automated distribution network with their operational expertise, technology, and integrated logistics capabilities,” Leibbrandt said. “This next phase of our partnership strengthens our ability to move products more efficiently across channels, improve responsiveness to changing demand, and create greater value from the investments we’ve made in our U.S. distribution infrastructure.”

Maersk currently operates more than 70 fulfillment facilities in North America. They total about 22.5 million square feet. Globally, it operates more than 500 warehouses spanning more than 100 million square feet.

Puma is No. 65 in the Europe Database. The market research tool tracks the region’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

What Maersk is doing with Puma’s distribution network

Maersk said it already provides warehousing and distribution logistics services to help Puma deliver to consumers worldwide. Those include:

  • Air freight
  • Customs services
  • Fulfillment
  • Inland transportation

The companies said the “next phase of their partnership” strengthens Puma’s U.S. distribution network. Maersk said it will help to maximize the performance of Puma’s automated facilities, improve efficiency and reduce costs. At the same time, it said, it will support orders for the apparel brand’s retail stores, online shoppers and wholesale customers.

Dave Hune, North America head of Maersk contract logistics, said in a statement that the company is working with Puma to create a more flexible and scalable fulfillment network. Together, he said, they seek to “keep products moving quickly to stores and consumers.”

“Many companies are looking for ways to get more value from the logistics infrastructure they’ve already invested in,” Hune said. “This partnership is a great example of how Maersk can combine our operational expertise, technology, and logistics network with a customer’s existing assets to improve efficiency, maximize the value of automation, and reduce costs.”

Maersk said it supports Puma with integrated logistics solutions. The former listed asset control and data visibility as “core benefits.”

How Puma and Maersk are using automated warehouse technology

Puma’s automated warehouses in Arizona, California and Indiana use a technology called AutoStore. Maersk described it as an automated storage and retrieval system combining automation and software “to enable more intelligent and efficient fulfillment.”

The process requires storing inventory in a compact grid for robots to automatically retrieve. The robots bring goods directly to employees at workstations for picking and packing. That reduces unnecessary travel and manual handling, according to Maersk. In turn, that improves speed, efficiency and workplace productivity “while making better use of available warehouse space.”

AutoStore’s design is flexible and scalable, Maersk said. That helps operations adapt to changing demand while maintaining fulfillment performance across ecommerce, retail and wholesale channels.

“The partnership advances Maersk’s strategy of delivering integrated logistics solutions that connect physical assets, transportation networks as well as the latest technology and digital assets to create greater operational control, reliability and value for customers,” Maersk said. “As supply chains become increasingly complex, fulfillment plays a growing role in helping businesses position inventory closer to demand, respond more quickly to market changes and serve consumers across channels.”

The California facility will also become Maersk’s first in North America to support multiple clients’ operations. Starting in 2027, Maersk said, it will have capacity in that facility, located in Torrance, “for other brands that need fast, automated order fulfillment near strategic air and ocean gateways as well as one of the largest consumer markets in the country.”

data.title: DoorDash expands access to agentic ordering for offices, corporate customers
data.description:
DoorDash put its latest artificial intelligence (AI), delivery and ordering options on display at its Dash Forward event in San Francisco on Tuesday, opening up agentic ordering to workplaces for new users.

In addition to showing off new drones and its Dasher Returns services, the last-mile delivery platform and marketplace named its first corporate customers for a connector-enabled option that is intended to let companies use their internally adopted AI tools to automate ordering for use cases such as lunch catering and office supplies replenishment.

Currently, access is only available through a waitlist, but DoorDash announced that SpaceX, Cognition, Vercel, Mercor and Tempo are all early partners putting the connector to use.

How does DoorDash’s agentic ordering to offices work?

Andy Fang, co-founder and director at DoorDash, noted on stage at the DoorDash headquarters that the company launched the command line interface in beta in July, setting up capabilities that make agentic ordering to workplaces possible. He said that the beta “enables individual developers to connect DoorDash ordering capabilities to their personal agents,” creating recurring grocery orders and discovering new options according to their preferences.

“In fact, one of the biggest use cases we saw was automating their office work,” Fang stated. “And so now, to make it easier for companies to put their office orders and office supply restocks on autopilot, we’re excited to introduce the DoorDash MCP for corporate ordering.”

MCP stands for Model Context Protocol, which is an open standard that lets external services connect to AI applications. DoorDash cited Slack as an example of an app where employees at an office might interact with a bot that uses the connector to place orders through DoorDash for delivery from local restaurants or merchants.

“Companies can now use it to bring agentic ordering into tools their teams are already working in, or give internal agents the ability to order through DoorDash,” he said. “And this opens up a ton of possibilities for companies to turn the tools that their teams are using every day into a way to get what they need delivered.”

Who has access to DoorDash MCP for corporate ordering?

DoorDash opened a waitlist to sign up for DoorDash MCP for corporate ordering on its developer site’s MCP page as of Sept. 30. Accepted participants gain access at the company level, with employees then required to sign in to individual DoorDash accounts to agree to terms of service and connect AI agents.

DoorDash noted that the beta is currently limited in scope as it grants companies access to place orders for their teams.

data.title: DoorDash prepares nationwide Returns service, welcomes new retailers to marketplace
data.description:
DoorDash unveiled its new service for returns, along with other new app features and retail partners using its marketplace on Sept. 29 at its Dash Forward event in San Francisco.

The last-mile delivery app, which recently added Costco deliveries in the U.S. and joined Lowe’s and Wing to pilot drone delivery, also showed off its own DoorDash Air drone at the event — though Air was announced for early use with its food delivery partners Chipotle and Popeyes.

DoorDash CEO and co-founder Tony Xu appeared on stage to discuss the company’s latest moves. Xu was joined by other DoorDash executives, as well as representatives from Macy’s, Chipotle and Popeyes.

Dasher Returns is currently launching in a limited number of cities, with a nationwide rollout planned for November, according to DoorDash.

How will DoorDash’s Dasher Returns work?

“Starting today, we’re launching Dasher Returns,” said Shanna Prevé, chief revenue officer at DoorDash. “For a flat fee, DoorDash will come to your home, pick up your return, and take it back to the store for you.” 

Prevé walked through a use case with an order from Gap as an example, demonstrating that a return request can be placed right away or scheduled. After someone accepts the request, they pick up the item and take it back to the merchant’s physical store.

“Because that inventory goes back on the shelves today, Gap has a chance to resell it to another mom, and I get my refund in days, not weeks,” she stated.

Prevé called the experience “the return experience I wish I always had.” The company expects to make 80% of the retail orders it handles eligible for Dasher Returns by the end of 2026.

New retailers in the DoorDash app

DoorDash operates its own marketplace within its app for retailers, whose products are searchable and often available for same-day delivery.

“There are more than 200,000 retailers and grocers available across Deliveroo, DoorDash and Bolt,” Prevé shared, naming two of DoorDash’s other platforms. “Every single one of these retailers has decided a customer shouldn’t have to choose between getting something fast and getting it from a brand they trust.”

The company named five new brands set to appear in the app.

“Today, we are adding to that list of brands with some of my favorites, including Anthropologie, North Face, Timberland, Vans and Macy’s,” she said.

Prevé welcomed Josh Janos, vice president of marketplaces and digital partnerships at Macy’s, to the stage, to discuss the department store’s decision to sell through DoorDash. Macy’s previously began working with DoorDash as a white-label same-day and next-day fulfillment service in 2020, using it for orders made through Macys.com, Macy’s mobile app and Bloomingdales.com.

“Now, today we are announcing that the Macy’s catalog will be available from within the DoorDash Marketplace app,” Janos said.

Together, the companies also announced that DoorDash would be participating in the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade on Nov. 26 in New York City.

Macy’s ranks No. 17 in Digital Commerce 360’s Top 2000 Database. The market research tool ranks the largest North American online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales.

AI tools and drone delivery

In addition to Dasher Returns, DoorDash detailed other new launches for customers and delivery workers on its platform. Those included:

  • DoorDash MCP for corporate ordering, connecting AI agents to DoorDash’s system
  • Text DoorDash, a system for ordering from DoorDash through text messages, currently open to users through a waitlist
  • Ask DoorDash, a conversational interface for shoppers
  • DashBuddy, a text-based SMS chatbot for delivery workers, which it refers to as Dashers, using the platform
  • DoorDash Air, which is entering use for some Chipotle and Popeyes food orders

Last, Stanley Tang, chief product officer and co-founder at DoorDash, offered an update on the company’s Dot delivery robots. The wheeled units debuted a year ago and have since continued to increase workloads. The robots currently traverse roads, bike lanes and sidewalks to complete orders.

“Today, Dot is scaling, making deliveries for over 2,000 store locations across Greater Phoenix, from local restaurants — like Grove and Real Cafe — to national chains like Little Caesars,” Tang said. “Each Dot is completing three times the number of deliveries compared to last year.”
